rubrics.justification: Describes a day-5 expanded/hatching blastocyst with B-grade ICM and A-grade TE consistent with 4BA; notes no obvious severe degeneration. Some image-specific details (e.g., 'tissue protruding toward the outer layer,' zona not extremely thinned) may be somewhat inferential from a static image.

Strong integration of maternal age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, first-cycle status, and male-factor semen parameters with embryo quality and prognosis, including how low motility may affect embryo competence despite good morphology.

Overall logic is structured and mostly consistent, but there is a notable contradiction: after estimating live birth at ~35–50%, the bottom line states 'mid-to-high teens percent per transfer.' Probability framing around euploid vs untested embryos is also somewhat muddled.

Generally aligns with Gardner grading concepts and mainstream IVF practice: reasonable transfer of a 4BA day-5 blastocyst, caution about add-ons, and nuanced discussion of PGT-A at age 31. Minor deviations include somewhat speculative emphasis on sperm DNA fragmentation without direct indication.

Provides practical recommendations for proceeding with transfer, optimizing luteal support/transfer technique, lifestyle advice, and future workup including review of fertilization/blastulation and possible male-factor evaluation. Useful, though some suggestions remain broad rather than protocol-specific.
